NOTABLE FINDING for this stratum, same shape as the sibling LA3D region of this batch: `next(response_graph.triples(expected_response_1))` is syntactically the trav_single_value idiom this region was sampled for, but `expected_response_1` is a FULLY BOUND triple -- all three terms known, zero variables. The value `next()` returns is never used for anything but its truthiness in the bare `assert`; there is no 'single value I expect' to bind, only a membership test. Per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 ('la construction la plus specifique'), the most specific construction is therefore trav_existence's `bool(m{ })` -- the exact worked example in querying.md#the-single-expected-value-and-existence (`assert bool(m{ ex:b a ex:Sensor })`) -- not `.first()`/`.one()`: this region contributes ZERO occurrences of `.first()`/`.one()` despite its stratum label.

`expected_response_1` (a plain tuple, used only as the argument to `.triples()`) was inlined directly into the `m{ }` pattern rather than kept as a separate variable: this is the notation's native form for a literal triple (every worked example in querying.md/migrate-from-rdflib.md writes the pattern in place, never builds a tuple first) and there is no island form for 'a Python tuple of terms used as a whole pattern' -- not a restructuring of control flow, just the direct spelling the doc itself uses for this exact shape.

zero-solution branch cannot be exercised through this driver: the entire function body IS the one `assert`, so a fixture where the triple is absent would make the ORIGINAL side raise inside `run_pair`'s single try/except, which aborts the whole comparison on the first side that raises rather than checking whether both sides raise alike (see rdfeval/harness.py) -- same limitation already documented on the sibling LA3D region of this batch. Hardened the fixture instead with neighbourhood data (a second Feature of the same type, a second type on the same subject) that must not satisfy the exact triple.

Repair 2026-10-30: `assert bool(m{ Feature1 rdf:type geo:Feature })` was not faithful when the triple is absent: the original raises StopIteration('') from `next()`, the translation raised AssertionError(''), and the harness compares raises (the note above that says it cannot is wrong). The strengthened driver shows it on four absent-triple graphs; the translation is now `assert next(iter(m{ ... })) is not None`, which raises the same StopIteration and passes when the triple is present.

Language observation: an m{ } that projects NO variable yields an empty `Row()`, which is falsy, so the literal rewrite `assert next(iter(m{ ... }))` fails on a PRESENT triple (verified: check FAIL on call 0). The `is not None` keeps the assert a no-op beyond the StopIteration, as the original's assert on a 3-tuple is.

Correction (2026-11-01, record corpus/403, defect 2): what this note says of run_pair is not true. run_pair compares a raise like a value — the same exception type and message on both sides, or a difference — and goes on with the next call; it never aborts the comparison on the first side that raises. A workaround described above stays valid, but is not needed.
